findings.evidence: `Complexification.lean:380` declares `(n : ℕ∞ω)` for `realPartLinearMap`, `conjEquiv` and `complexificationEquivProd`. `Section/Support.lean:43` declares `{n : ℕ∞ω}` for `supportedIn`, `compactlySupported` and `ofSupportedIn`.
findings.fix: Use `{n : ℕ∞ω}` in this section, matching the surrounding `ComplexificationSections` API. Keep `ℕ∞` only in the topology file, where chart finality requires it.
findings.issue: `section SupportedComplexificationSections` uses `variable {n : ℕ∞}`, so `CompactlySupported.realPart/imaginaryPart/oneTmul/ITmul`, `complexificationEquivProd`, the `SupportedIn.*` equivalences, `realPointsConj(Equiv)` and the support laws all exclude `ω`. Nothing in these algebraic proofs needs finite or `∞` regularity.

findings.evidence: `Complexification.lean:454` already gives `conjEquiv` on all sections via `fun x ↦ tmulConj (E x) (σ x)`. The proofs of `tsupport_conjCLE` and `conjCLE_involutive` use only `conjCLE_apply` and `tmulConj_tmulConj`, never the topology.
findings.fix: In `Complexification.lean`, restrict the existing `ContMDiffSection.conjEquiv` and the native `ℂ`-smul to `compactlySupported` and `supportedIn` as real linear equivalences, with no topology. Prove the apply, support, involution and square laws there, ideally with a tsupport law for `conjEquiv` on all sections. Then build `conjCLE` and `smulICLE` by adding continuity only.
findings.issue: Fibrewise multiplication by `i` and conjugation are defined only as `smulICLE` and `conjCLE`, through `complexificationCLEProd`. Their purely algebraic laws (`conjCLE_apply`, `smulICLE_apply`, `tsupport_conjCLE`, `tsupport_smulICLE`, `conjCLE_involutive`, `smulICLE_smulICLE`) therefore require `FiniteDimensional`, `Boundaryless`, `T2`, `SigmaCompact`, `IsManifold I ∞` and an `e`/`U`/`hU`/`hcover` cover that the statements never use.

summary: The algebraic support and comparison layer is stated for `n : ℕ∞` although every native ingredient works at `ℕ∞ω`. The fibrewise conjugation and quarter-turn laws are proved only for CLEs that carry the full chart-finality hypotheses, although the statements are purely algebraic.
